title: Workflow Execution Robustness — Host-and-Layout Compatibility
overview: Running /project-orchestrate end-to-end against a repo whose node_modules is untracked (stolarch) surfaced two independent, structural defects in the v2.0.0 Workflow scripts under lib/workflows/. Defect 1: args normalization is missing across EVERY workflow — all four entry points (review_panel.js:47, adversarial_verify.js:47, elaborate_epics.js:62, sprint_pipeline.js:127-138) destructure the injected `args` global directly, so a host that delivers `args` as a JSON string silently yields undefined for every field. The fix is a single shared normalizeArgs(raw, workflowName) with a HARD contract: non-null non-array object passes through by same reference; a string is JSON.parse'd in try/catch and throws WITH CONTEXT (naming the workflow) on malformed JSON; after any parse the result is ASSERTED to be a non-null non-array object (so '[]', '42', '"x"', 'null' THROW, closing the silent-undefined cascade); null/undefined/array/primitive THROW (no implicit {} default); double-encoded strings are re-parsed then re-asserted, never handed to the destructure. DELIVERY MECHANISM (applies to ALL _shared modules, not just the normalizer): the scripts run in a wrapped-eval runtime (proven by co-existing top-level `export const meta` at sprint_pipeline.js:47, top-level `return` at :142/:360, and top-level `await` at adversarial_verify.js:141 — jointly illegal in real ESM/CJS), so a static `import` declaration is a likely SyntaxError; top-level await IS supported, so every consumer obtains each canonical module via dynamic `await import('./_shared/<module>.mjs')`. EVERY such `await import(...)` MUST be wrapped to FAIL LOUD with a diagnostic naming the SPECIFIC module and the workflow — and because each runs before any per-story .catch isolation, ANY one unresolvable _shared module aborts the WHOLE invocation. The import surface is now ×4 canonical helpers (normalize_args consumed by all four scripts; detect_repo_layout, topological_order, reset_worktree consumed by sprint_pipeline.js) PLUS the extracted sequential driver (×5). This blast radius is declared ACCEPTABLE and preferable to silent-undefined, CONTINGENT on Open Spike S2 resolving positively. If S2 resolves negative, the named fallback is installer-codegen-from-single-source applied to ALL modules (the installer inlines each one canonical source into every consuming script at copy time, preserving DRY at the source level); the fallback is contingent and currently has NO automated E-coverage (a known risk to close if S2 goes negative). S2 is a HARD GATE on the mechanism. Module names are pinned to .mjs (explicit ESM on all Node versions — no CJS-default reparse, no MODULE_TYPELESS warning, no Node<22.7 SyntaxError). PACKAGING: bin/install.js:122 copies recursively (copyRecursive), so lib/workflows/_shared/ ships automatically — NO new copy step. But copyRecursive (install.js:149-161) copies every file verbatim and this spec COLOCATES *.test.mjs beside each module (house style, CLAUDE.md §1.7); verbatim-copy + colocated-tests + 'no installer change' cannot all hold, so a MINIMAL installer change is REQUIRED: generalize copyRecursive's single skipPath parameter into a skip PREDICATE and skip any *.test.* during the workflow copy (the earlier 'no installer change for tests' claim is RETRACTED). The post-install smoke check asserts _shared/*.mjs are present/importable AND no *.test.* shipped. Defect 2: sprint_pipeline.js runs Implement (301) and Verify (317) agents in fresh git worktrees (isolation:'worktree'); a fresh `git worktree add` materializes TRACKED files only, so gitignored node_modules is absent regardless of hoisting and every tsc/jest fails. The CORRECT detection axis is node_modules TRACKED vs UNTRACKED (NOT hoisted vs non-hoisted): `git ls-files node_modules` NON-EMPTY stdout -> tracked -> worktree-safe; EMPTY stdout (exit 0, there is NO exit-1 'no' case) -> untracked -> serial-in-tree; not-a-git-repo/command-error (git exit 128, caught) -> serial-in-tree (safe default). The safe path is the COMMON path. Serial-in-tree design: execute stories FULLY SEQUENTIALLY in a GENUINE dependency-topological order (Kahn's algorithm over in-batch blockers — NET-NEW logic, NOT array order; throws on a cycle; a naive array-order serialization would re-deadlock at sprint_pipeline.js:289 when a dependent precedes its blocker), driven by an EXTRACTED, unit-testable sequential driver runSequential(orderedStories, { runChain, resetBetween }) that runs exactly ONE chain in flight, awaits each story's full impl->review->verify->merge chain before the next, and runs the reset BETWEEN stories (after N's merge is captured, before N+1's checkout, never after the last) — and MUST NOT reintroduce a lock before the dependency-await at line 289 (a 'serialize behind a lock' reading re-creates the R2 deadlock and is explicitly the wrong approach). Zero concurrency dissolves the shared-HEAD race (R1) and REMOVES the shared-tree lock entirely (R2). The DEPENDENCY-PRESERVING between-story reset runs in this EXACT order: `git reset --hard` -> `git checkout -f <releaseBranch>` -> `git clean -fdx -e node_modules -e '**/node_modules'`. ORDER MATTERS: reset --hard runs FIRST to discard conflicting uncommitted tracked changes a failed/aborted Implement left behind, so the subsequent checkout cannot abort on a dirty tree (the earlier checkout->reset order was WRONG for exactly the aborted-Implement case). A bare `git clean -fdx` is FORBIDDEN (its -x deletes the untracked node_modules serial-in-tree exists to reuse, re-inflicting Defect 2 every story); the `-e '**/node_modules'` exclude is REDUNDANT (a no-slash `node_modules` exclude already matches at ANY depth per gitignore pathspec semantics) — kept as harmless belt-and-suspenders, NOT 'required for nested' (that justification was false); `git stash` is NOT equivalent (excludes ignored files by default). The reset must revert tracked changes AND clear stray build artifacts (dist/, coverage) while PRESERVING every node_modules (root + nested), including after a failed/aborted Implement left the tree dirty (R3). Worktree mode is BEHAVIORALLY unchanged (source is not byte-identical — isolationStrategy is threaded through runStory and the Implement/Verify prompts become conditional at 179/200); the file now hosts TWO execution models (parallel-worktree, sequential-in-tree) that must NEVER be mixed mid-run. An HONEST OPTIONAL override — isolationStrategy?: 'auto'|'worktree'|'serial-in-tree' (default 'auto', token exactly 'serial-in-tree', NO 'serial' short form, NO env var) — lets an operator force a strategy; existing 10-arg callers keep working. Forcing 'worktree' on untracked node_modules emits a prominent log() WARNING then warns-and-proceeds. skills/project-orchestrate/SKILL.md MUST be updated (the 'SKILL.md untouched' claim is RETRACTED): add the optional isolationStrategy to the args block (405-416) and HOLISTICALLY reconcile the stale paragraph (428-432) — the 'always run in isolated git worktrees', 'min(16, cpu_cores-2)' concurrency (line 430), and 'serialized behind a lock' (line 432) claims are ALL now mode-conditional (false under serial-in-tree). COST: serial-in-tree is ~N× wall-clock vs min(16, cores-2) concurrency from LOST PARALLELISM only — the reset preserves node_modules so there is NO per-story reinstall (zero extra install cost); an accepted correctness-over-speed tradeoff on the COMMON repo shape. TWO OPEN SPIKES GATE ALL IMPLEMENTATION and are encoded as the FIRST epic (runtime-behavior-spikes) on which every other epic depends (design_spike: true): S1 — what this runtime's isolation:'worktree' does with untracked files (if it OVERLAYS the live tree including untracked node_modules, Defect 2 largely evaporates and the detector + serial-in-tree work — F5/F6/F7*/F8/F9*/F10 and E2-E5 — become NO-OPS, collapsing the repo-layout-detection and serial-in-tree-execution epics to near-empty; only args normalization survives); S2 — dynamic-import relative-specifier resolution for ALL _shared/*.mjs in source and installed layouts (hard gate on the delivery mechanism; else the F2b codegen fallback for all modules). No feature code starts until S1 and S2 are resolved. VERIFICATION refactors for testability instead of rebuilding the runtime: the risky logic is EXTRACTED into small pure/near-pure importable .mjs modules under lib/workflows/_shared/ (normalizeArgs; detectIsolationStrategy(repoRoot); the topological-ordering function; the tree-reset routine; the sequential driver) so E1 (normalizer) + E2 (detector) + E3 (topo-sort incl. adverse order + cycle throw) + E4 (tree-reset: a GENUINELY CONFLICTING dirty tracked file, then clean tree + node_modules survives + dist/ cleared) + E5 (sequential driver: order = topo order, single-in-flight, reset between every adjacent pair and not after the last, termination on adverse pair) are AUTOMATED unit tests via `node --test` against REAL git in temp dirs. E5 converts the concurrency-safety guarantee from manual-only to automated, mitigating the M1-skip risk. The FULL sprint_pipeline end-to-end run (real Workflow runtime, real >=2-story serial batch) becomes a DOCUMENTED MANUAL gate (M1) with EXACT steps. Reconstructing/replicating the wrapped-eval Workflow runtime in a test harness is an explicit NON-GOAL. Test ownership is single-owner: E1 -> args epic; E2 -> detection epic; E3+E4+E5 -> execution epic; integration + M1 -> emulation epic. Note: github-mode cross-story dependency chaining (a dependent branching from releaseBranch that lacks a blocker's un-merged PR commits) is PRE-EXISTING and NOT regressed by serial-in-tree; it is out of scope and must not be rediscovered as a new defect.

primary: Resolve the two gating runtime spikes FIRST (runtime-behavior-spikes epic, design_spike): S1 — does isolation:'worktree' overlay untracked files (if so the detector + serial-in-tree work largely evaporate and scope collapses)? S2 — does relative-specifier `await import()` resolve for ALL _shared/*.mjs in both source and installed layouts? No feature implementation begins until both are resolved; the gating is enforced by epic depends_on edges, not narrative.

Make every workflow host-delivery agnostic: all four entry points obtain one shared normalizeArgs via a FAIL-LOUD dynamic `await import('./_shared/normalize_args.mjs')` and read inputs through it. The contract FAILS LOUD — object passthrough by same reference; malformed JSON throws with context; post-parse object assertion so '[]'/'42'/'null'/primitives throw; no implicit {} default; double-encoded re-parsed. EVERY _shared import (normalizer + sprint_pipeline's detector/topo/reset/driver) is wrapped so an unresolvable module throws a diagnostic naming THAT module and the workflow (blast radius = the whole invocation; acceptable, contingent on Spike S2; ×5 surface).

Make sprint_pipeline.js layout-aware on the CORRECT axis: detect whether node_modules is TRACKED (survives into a fresh worktree via `git ls-files node_modules`, non-empty stdout) and choose isolation:'worktree' vs serial-in-tree accordingly, with serial-in-tree as the common, safe path. In serial-in-tree mode, run stories in a GENUINE dependency-topological order (Kahn's algorithm, net-new logic, throws on a cycle), NEVER array order, driven by an extracted testable sequential driver that runs exactly one story chain in flight.

Prove both fixes by testing EXTRACTED logic, not by rebuilding the runtime: normalizer, detector, topological-ordering, between-story tree-reset, and the sequential driver are extracted into small importable .mjs modules and covered by AUTOMATED unit tests (`node --test`) against REAL git in temp dirs (E1-E5). The full sprint_pipeline end-to-end run (real Workflow runtime, real >=2-story serial batch) is a DOCUMENTED MANUAL gate (M1) with exact steps — not an automated CI harness. Reconstructing the wrapped-eval runtime in a harness is a NON-GOAL.
secondary: Honor DRY: exactly one normalizeArgs, one layout detector, one topological-ordering function, one tree-reset routine, and one sequential driver, delivered via `await import()`; zero per-file shims (CLAUDE.md §1.4 — the `= args` pattern already recurs four times).
Fail safe on ambiguity and on error: unknown/inconclusive layouts AND detector command-errors default to serial-in-tree; a detector throw must NEVER kill the batch.

Keep packaging honest: the recursive copy at bin/install.js:122 ships _shared/ automatically, but a MINIMAL installer change is REQUIRED — generalize copyRecursive's skipPath into a skip predicate that filters *.test.* so colocated tests do NOT ship; a post-install smoke check asserts _shared/*.mjs present/importable AND no *.test.* shipped. The 'no installer change for tests' claim is RETRACTED; the only OTHER contingent installer edit is the S2-negative codegen fallback.

Preserve sprint_pipeline.js's single-writer-of-the-working-tree invariant (header lines 8-21) under serial-in-tree by executing stories fully sequentially — not by adding a lock (any lock ahead of the dependency-await at line 289 would deadlock; serial-in-tree REMOVES the lock entirely and the sequential driver must not reintroduce one).

Provide an HONEST OPTIONAL override — isolationStrategy?: 'auto'|'worktree'|'serial-in-tree' (default 'auto', no 'serial' short form, no env var) — so existing 10-arg callers keep working and an operator can force a strategy; guard the forced-'worktree'-over-untracked-deps foot-gun with a prominent warning, and update skills/project-orchestrate/SKILL.md (args block + holistic reconciliation of the stale worktrees/concurrency/lock paragraph).

epics.name: Runtime-behavior spikes
epics.description: GATING epic — resolves the two runtime spikes that block all feature implementation; every other epic depends_on this one and the plan carries design_spike: true. S1 (gates Defect 2): confirm what THIS Workflow runtime's isolation:'worktree' does with untracked files. If it performs a plain `git worktree add` (TRACKED files only), the detector is required as specified and serial-in-tree is required for untracked-node_modules repos. If it COPIES/OVERLAYS the live working tree (untracked files INCLUDED, e.g. node_modules), Defect 2 LARGELY EVAPORATES and downstream scope COLLAPSES: the detector (detect_repo_layout.mjs; F8/F9/F9a/F10), the serial-in-tree strategy and its topological order/reset/sequential driver (F7/F7a/F7b/F7c/F7d), the optional override and SKILL.md reconciliation (F9b/F9c), and E2-E5 all become NO-OPS / are not built — the repo-layout-detection and serial-in-tree-execution epics shrink to near-empty and only args normalization (F1-F3, E1) plus its verification remain. The plan MUST branch on this finding BEFORE building the detector. S2 (hard gate on the Defect 1 mechanism): confirm dynamic-import relative-specifier resolution ('./_shared/<module>.mjs') works in the wrapped-eval runtime for EVERY _shared/*.mjs (normalizer, detector, topological order, reset, sequential driver), in BOTH the source tree and the installed <skills-root>/_workflows/ layout, BEFORE wiring any entry point. If unreliable, resolve against a runtime-provided base if one exists; else adopt installer-codegen-from-single-source (F2b) for ALL modules — a fallback that is contingent and currently has NO automated E-coverage (a known risk to close if S2 goes negative). This epic produces the resolved findings and the branch decision; it does not itself ship feature code.
shared_design_concerns: S1 and S2 are GATING acceptance items, not footnotes: no feature implementation starts until both are resolved, and the gating is enforced by the depends_on edges from every other epic to this one.

S1 scope-collapse: if the runtime overlays untracked files into worktrees, F5/F6/F7/F7a/F7b/F7c/F7d/F8/F9/F9a/F9b/F9c/F10 and E2-E5 become no-ops; the repo-layout-detection and serial-in-tree-execution epics collapse to near-empty; only args normalization (F1-F3, E1) and its verification remain. The plan must branch on the finding before building the detector.

S2 covers relative-specifier resolution for ALL _shared/*.mjs (normalizer, detector, topological order, reset, sequential driver), in source AND installed layouts. It is a hard gate on the delivery mechanism.

S2-negative fallback is installer-codegen-from-single-source for ALL modules (each one canonical source inlined into its consuming scripts at copy time; DRY preserved at source level). The fallback is contingent and has NO automated E-coverage — flag as a known risk if S2 goes negative.
This epic BLOCKS args-normalization-extraction, repo-layout-detection, serial-in-tree-execution, and (transitively) end-to-end-emulation-and-verification.

epics.name: Args-normalization extraction
epics.description: Create one shared lib/workflows/_shared/normalize_args.mjs exporting normalizeArgs(raw, workflowName) with a HARD, fail-loud contract and route ALL four workflow entry points through it via a FAIL-LOUD dynamic `await import()`. DELIVERY: the scripts run in a wrapped-eval runtime (top-level export const meta + top-level return + top-level await coexist — jointly illegal in real ESM/CJS), so a static `import` declaration is a likely SyntaxError; top-level await is supported, so use `const { normalizeArgs } = await import('./_shared/normalize_args.mjs')` in all four (review_panel.js:47, adversarial_verify.js:47, elaborate_epics.js:62, sprint_pipeline.js:127-138) and destructure from normalizeArgs(args, '<name>'). The `await import(...)` MUST be WRAPPED to fail loud with a diagnostic naming the specific module and the workflow; because it runs before any per-story .catch isolation, an import failure aborts the WHOLE invocation — declared ACCEPTABLE and preferable to silent-undefined, CONTINGENT on Open Spike S2 (resolved in the runtime-behavior-spikes epic). Module name is pinned to .mjs (explicit ESM on all Node versions). PACKAGING/INSTALLER (owned here as the first epic to introduce a colocated test): bin/install.js:122 copies _shared/ recursively — no new copy step — but copyRecursive (install.js:149-161) copies every file verbatim, so a MINIMAL installer change is REQUIRED to keep colocated *.test.mjs out of the payload: generalize copyRecursive's single skipPath parameter into a skip PREDICATE and skip any *.test.* during the workflow copy (the 'no installer change for tests' claim is RETRACTED). Add a post-install smoke check that <skills-root>/_workflows/_shared/normalize_args.mjs is present/importable AND that no *.test.* shipped. UNIT TEST (E1, owned here): colocate normalize_args.test.mjs covering object passthrough (same reference), JSON-string-of-object, '[]', '42', null, undefined, malformed string, and double-encoded — good shapes pass, every bad shape THROWS with context.
shared_design_concerns: Exactly one authoritative definition of the string-or-object contract; a copy-pasted shim in each file violates CLAUDE.md §1.4.
Object passthrough must return the SAME reference (no clone) to preserve current behavior on hosts that already deliver an object.

Fail loud, never default: malformed JSON, post-parse non-objects ('[]'/'42'/'null'/primitives), null/undefined/array, and double-encoded strings must throw with context naming the workflow — never a silent undefined and never an implicit {}.

Delivery is a FAIL-LOUD dynamic `await import()`, NOT a static import declaration, because the wrapped-eval runtime (co-existing top-level export/return/await) would treat a static import as a likely SyntaxError. The import is wrapped so an unresolvable module throws a diagnostic naming the module and the workflow.

Import blast radius: the top-level `await import(...)` runs before per-story .catch isolation, so a failed import aborts the WHOLE invocation. This is declared ACCEPTABLE and better than silent-undefined, CONTINGENT on Spike S2 (resolved upstream in runtime-behavior-spikes).
Pin the module format to .mjs (explicit ESM on all Node versions); update all references — import specifier and unit test — to the .mjs path.

Installer change (owned here): the recursive copyRecursive at bin/install.js:122 ships _shared/ but copies every file verbatim; generalize its single skipPath into a skip PREDICATE and filter *.test.* so colocated tests do NOT ship. Verify via a post-install smoke check (modules present/importable, no *.test.* shipped). The only other contingent installer edit is the S2-negative codegen fallback.
E1 (owned here): the normalizer fail-loud matrix is this epic's colocated unit test; the emulation epic does NOT re-author it.

epics.name: Repo-layout detection

A fresh `git worktree add` materializes TRACKED files only, so gitignored node_modules is absent regardless of workspace hoisting or pnpm. Heuristic: `git ls-files node_modules` NON-EMPTY stdout -> tracked/vendored -> worktree-safe; EMPTY stdout (exit 0 — there is NO exit-1 'no' case) -> untracked -> serial-in-tree; not-a-git-repo/command-error (git exit 128, caught) -> serial-in-tree (safe default). Branch on empty-vs-nonempty stdout; reserve try/catch for the command-error case only; a detector throw NEVER kills the batch. The safe path is the COMMON path — most single-package repos AND monorepos leave node_modules untracked; worktree is the rare vendored-deps case. Detect ONCE after the empty-batch guard (currently lines 140-143), honoring an HONEST OPTIONAL override first (isolationStrategy?: 'auto'|'worktree'|'serial-in-tree', default 'auto', token exactly 'serial-in-tree', NO 'serial' short form, NO env var — optional with 'auto' default so existing 10-arg callers keep working), else calling the detector; log the strategy, the evidence (git ls-files stdout: empty/non-empty/command-error), and whether it came from auto or override (F10). Forcing 'worktree' while detection finds untracked node_modules emits a prominent log() WARNING that deps must already exist in the worktree or the build fails, then warns-and-proceeds. runStory (lines 286-332) reads that single value when setting isolation on the Implement agent (301) and Verify agent (317). SKILL.md reconciliation (owned here; the 'SKILL.md untouched' claim is RETRACTED): update skills/project-orchestrate/SKILL.md to add the optional isolationStrategy to the args block (405-416) and HOLISTICALLY reconcile the stale paragraph at 428-432 — the 'always run in isolated git worktrees' claim, the 'min(16, cpu_cores-2)' concurrency claim (line 430), and the 'serialized behind a lock' claim (line 432) are ALL now mode-conditional (false under serial-in-tree) and must be rewritten to reflect the two execution models. UNIT TEST (E2, owned here): colocate detect_repo_layout.test.mjs per branch against real temp repos — tracked -> worktree, untracked -> serial-in-tree, non-git/command-error -> serial-in-tree (never throws to the caller). This epic edits sprint_pipeline.js AFTER args-normalization-extraction so the file's edits are serialized (no parallel-worktree collision).
shared_design_concerns: Detection axis is node_modules TRACKED vs UNTRACKED via `git ls-files node_modules` — NOT hoisted vs non-hoisted, and there is no 'workspaces -> worktree-OK' fast path (a fresh worktree materializes tracked files only, so hoisting is irrelevant).

Correct exit-code handling: `git ls-files node_modules` exits 0 with EMPTY stdout when nothing is tracked (there is NO exit-1 'no' case). Branch on empty-vs-nonempty stdout (non-empty -> worktree, empty -> serial-in-tree); reserve try/catch for the command-error case only (non-git / git exit 128 -> serial-in-tree). A detector throw NEVER kills the batch.

The safe serial-in-tree path is the COMMON path (most single-package repos and monorepos leave node_modules untracked); worktree is the rare vendored-deps case. Do not frame worktree as the common/fast default that 'works fine today'.

HONEST OPTIONAL override: isolationStrategy?: 'auto'|'worktree'|'serial-in-tree' (default 'auto', token exactly 'serial-in-tree', NO 'serial' short form, NO env var). Optional with an 'auto' default so existing 10-arg callers keep working. Forcing 'worktree' on untracked node_modules must emit a prominent log() warning (deps must already exist or the build fails) and warn-and-proceed; the safe auto default remains serial-in-tree.

SKILL.md reconciliation (owned here; the 'SKILL.md untouched' claim is RETRACTED): add the optional isolationStrategy to the args block (405-416) and HOLISTICALLY reconcile the stale paragraph (428-432) — 'always run in isolated git worktrees', 'min(16, cpu_cores-2)' (line 430), and 'serialized behind a lock' (line 432) are ALL mode-conditional now and must be rewritten for the two execution models.
Log the strategy, the evidence (git ls-files stdout: empty/non-empty/command-error), and the source (auto detection vs override) so a wrong classification is diagnosable.

Extract testability: detectIsolationStrategy(repoRoot) in detect_repo_layout.mjs is a small importable .mjs module unit-testable against REAL git in temp dirs — no wrapped-eval runtime required. Any _shared module using ESM syntax must be .mjs.
E2 (owned here): the detector branch matrix is this epic's colocated unit test; the emulation epic does NOT re-author it.
This epic edits sprint_pipeline.js only after args-normalization-extraction (linear DAG), so no two concurrently-editable epics touch the file.
